title: OCD Treatment: What Actually Works (Evidence-Based Guide)
description: The gold standard treatment for OCD is ERP therapy, not just any therapy. How it works, what to expect, medication options, and finding specialized help.

content.text: OCD is one of the most treatable mental health conditions—but only with the right treatment. Here's what actually works.
Why Regular Therapy Often Fails OCD

Traditional talk therapy can actually make OCD worse. Discussing fears and seeking reassurance feeds the OCD cycle. The effective treatment is counterintuitive: you have to face the fears without doing compulsions.
Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is the first-line treatment for OCD:
ERP produces significant improvement in 60-80% of patients who complete treatment, with effects lasting years.

items: Response Prevention: Resisting the urge to do compulsions
Habituation: Anxiety naturally decreases over time
Learning: Your brain learns the feared outcome doesn't happen
Notice it decreases on its own

content.text: ERP is hard—you're deliberately triggering anxiety. But the discomfort is temporary, and the freedom is lasting.

items: Fluoxetine, sertraline, fluvoxamine are FDA-approved for OCD
Higher doses often needed than for depression
Takes 8-12 weeks for full effect (longer than depression)

content.text: If SSRIs don't work fully, adding low-dose antipsychotics (risperidone, aripiprazole) helps some patients.

items: Combination may be best for severe OCD
Many can taper medication after successful ERP

content.text: Most therapists are NOT trained in ERP. Seeing a non-specialist can waste months and money. Look specifically for OCD specialists.

items: Ask: 'Do you do ERP?' If they say 'What's that?'—find someone else

content.text: OCD is highly treatable, but the treatment is specific: ERP, possibly with medication. Regular therapy often makes things worse. Find an OCD specialist, commit to the uncomfortable work of ERP, and you can reclaim your life from OCD.
